sentences.zh: 他的办公室里有一张大地图，上面标着他建成的所有东西，但也标着所有他没能建成的东西。

sentences.en: And he just has so many dreams and no one will ever be able to build them the way he could.
sentences.zh: 他有太多的梦想，而再也没人能像他那样去实现它们了。

sentences.en: Only someone would allow him to build them for the first time.
sentences.zh: 只要有人能允许他第一次去建造它们。

sentences.en: He needs someone's permission, someone's allowance to do it.
sentences.zh: 他需要某人的许可，某人的准许才能去做。

sentences.en: And he's frustrated that there's all these problems in the city and I'm necessary.
sentences.zh: 他很沮丧，因为城市里有这么多问题，而我是必要的。

sentences.en: I'm the only one who can solve it.
sentences.zh: 我是唯一能解决这些问题的人。

sentences.en: No one's asking me to do it.
sentences.zh: 没人找我去做。

sentences.en: I just I just don't understand.
sentences.zh: 我只是……我就是不明白。

sentences.en: And any attempt to rebuild his power is blocked by the mayor or the governor.
sentences.zh: 而任何重建权力的尝试都被市长或州长阻挠了。

sentences.en: And he starts getting angry.
sentences.zh: 他开始变得愤怒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's one point where he gets offers to write his memoirs.
sentences.zh: 有一次他收到邀请去写回忆录。

sentences.en: And it's like, I can't my life is built on secrets.
sentences.zh: 他觉得，不行，我的人生建立在秘密之上。

sentences.en: Like I can't write my memoirs.
sentences.zh: 我没法写回忆录。

sentences.en: So he puts out a book called Public Works, A Dangerous Trade, which I think is a very funny title.
sentences.zh: 于是他出了一本书叫《公共工程：危险的行业》（Public Works, A Dangerous Trade），我觉得这个书名很有趣。

sentences.en: And it's a 952 page book that mostly collects speeches and articles and letters.
sentences.zh: 那是一本952页的书，主要收集了演讲、文章和信件。

sentences.en: Like it's Kara refers to it as a non-book.
sentences.zh: 卡罗把它称为“非书”。

sentences.en: That's brutal.
sentences.zh: 这评价太狠了。

sentences.en: Kara's book is longer than that book, but it's full of things.
sentences.zh: 卡罗的书比那本还厚，但里面全是干货。

sentences.en: It's full of stuff.
sentences.zh: 全是内容。

sentences.en: You know, it's full of actual information.
sentences.zh: 你知道，全是实实在在的信息。

sentences.en: But it's brutal to be like, yeah, he released a non-book.
sentences.zh: 但说他发布了一本“非书”，这太残忍了。

sentences.en: But that title, Public Works, A Dangerous Trade, is really funny.
sentences.zh: 不过那个书名《公共工程：危险的行业》真的很有趣。

sentences.en: It is so good.
sentences.zh: 确实太棒了。

sentences.en: And he's so restless.
sentences.zh: 他非常焦躁不安。

sentences.en: This is the guy whose whole life was about getting things done.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个一生都在追求“把事情办成”的人。

sentences.en: And now he is literally incapable of getting things done.
sentences.zh: 而现在他实际上已经没有能力办成任何事了。

sentences.en: And the only trappings of power he still has is the guys who used to work with him, who are still loyal to him, still treat him like a big man.
sentences.zh: 他仅存的权力外衣就是那些曾经与他共事的人，他们依然忠于他，依然把他当大人物看。

sentences.en: George Spargo, who Moses makes up with, they keep their distance a little bit, even though he's still around.
sentences.zh: 乔治·斯帕戈（George Spargo），摩西与他重归于好，尽管他还在身边，但他们还是保持了一点距离。

sentences.en: But at park facilities, for a long time, they still treat him like an important person because the people running the parks came up under Moses for a certain amount of time.
sentences.zh: 但在公园管理部门，很长一段时间里，他们依然把他当重要人物，因为管理公园的人在摩西手下工作过一段时间。

sentences.en: And there's this one, another one of these Karo-specific scenarios that I really like.
sentences.zh: 还有一个卡罗特有的场景，我非常喜欢。

sentences.en: When the author drove him down to meet Adam Karp, Moses told him to park in an area marked No Thoroughfare.
sentences.zh: 当作者开车送他去见亚当·卡普（Adam Karp）时，摩西让他停在一个标有“禁止通行”的地方。

sentences.en: After he left, the author was sitting there jotting down notes when a Long Island State Park Commission patrolman loomed in his window.
sentences.zh: 他离开后，作者坐在车里记笔记，这时一名长岛州立公园委员会（LISPC）的巡警出现在车窗边。

sentences.en: Don't you see the sign?
sentences.zh: 你没看见那个牌子吗？

sentences.en: He asked with the usual LISPC arrogance.
sentences.zh: 他带着LISPC惯有的傲慢问道。

sentences.en: Well, you see, I drove Mr. Moses down, the author began.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你看，我是送摩西先生过来的，作者开始解释。

sentences.en: Oh, the cop said, straightening and started to walk away without a word.
sentences.zh: 哦，警察说，挺直了身子，一言不发地走开了。

sentences.en: Then he returned.
sentences.zh: 然后他又回来了。

sentences.en: Thanks for telling me, he said.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你告诉我，他说。

sentences.en: I'd be out of work and my children would be starving.
sentences.zh: 不然我就要丢掉工作，我的孩子们就要挨饿了。

sentences.en: So there's still this, the one thing that's outlasted him is fear, I guess, which stinks.
sentences.zh: 所以依然存在这种……唯一比他活得久的东西就是恐惧，我想，这真糟糕。

sentences.en: Yeah, for real.
sentences.zh: 确实，真的。

sentences.en: Moses is now the boogeyman you tell Long Island State Patrolman, State Parks Patrolman, to get them to let you park somewhere.
sentences.zh: 摩西现在成了你用来吓唬长岛州立公园巡警的“怪物”，好让他们让你停车。

sentences.en: So, oh, let me park here.
sentences.zh: 所以，哦，让我停在这儿吧。

sentences.en: Moses is going to come and take your children away.
sentences.zh: 摩西要来把你孩子带走了。

sentences.en: Like that's, it's not a great thing.
sentences.zh: 这可不是什么好事。

sentences.en: And during this period of time, you know, after that flurry of, you know, being named after things right when he like left his state posts, it's kind of gone fallow.
sentences.zh: 在那段时间里，你知道，在他离开州政府职位后，那一阵以他名字命名事物的热潮过后，一切都荒废了。

sentences.en: There's not a big Robert Moses State Park in Flushing Meadows.
sentences.zh: 法拉盛草原公园（Flushing Meadows）里并没有一个巨大的罗伯特·摩西州立公园。

sentences.en: There is a dedication because the plaza that he kind of cleared for Fordham gets named after him.
sentences.zh: 确实有一个落成仪式，因为他为福特汉姆大学（Fordham）清理出的广场以他的名字命名了。

sentences.en: But it feels kind of hollow because that's a private institution, you know, that doesn't.
sentences.zh: 但这感觉有点空洞，因为那是一个私立机构，你知道，那不算什么。

sentences.en: It's like a plaza on a college campus.
sentences.zh: 就像大学校园里的一个广场。

sentences.en: This is like not as exciting as like a major park that people are going to use.
sentences.zh: 这不像人们会去使用的大型公园那样令人兴奋。

sentences.en: I mean, and I don't know when they renamed Fire Island Robert Moses State Park.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道他们是什么时候把火岛改名为罗伯特·摩西州立公园的。

sentences.en: That must have been years later, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想那一定是多年以后的事了。

sentences.en: I should have looked that up ahead of time, but I didn't.
sentences.zh: 我本该提前查一下的，但我没查。

sentences.en: But you're right.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的。

sentences.en: He's, he's, there's this kind of trickling out of respect for him.
sentences.zh: 他……人们对他的尊重正在一点点流失。

sentences.en: Like in the late 60s and early 70s, he's still giving speeches and getting awards.
sentences.zh: 比如在60年代末和70年代初，他还在发表演讲并获得奖项。

sentences.en: By 1972, nobody really cares about him anymore.
sentences.zh: 到了1972年，真的没人再关心他了。

sentences.en: And they have a ceremony for the opening of a part of Lincoln Center that he fought for.
sentences.zh: 林肯中心（Lincoln Center）部分区域开幕时举行了仪式，那是他争取来的。

sentences.en: And he's like not even part of the ceremony.
sentences.zh: 但他甚至没能参加仪式。

sentences.en: Like there's no place for him, invited place for him on the dais.
sentences.zh: 主席台上根本没有留给他的位置。

sentences.en: Like he feels very insulted.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常受辱。

sentences.en: And Lindsay, who is still mayor, is using Moses' name as like this talisman of everything that was wrong with the city before Lindsay became mayor.
sentences.zh: 而当时依然在任的市长林赛（Lindsay），把摩西的名字当作一种护身符，用来指代林赛当选前城市里所有错误的东西。

sentences.en: And often, as Carol points out, because Carol can't help but get a dig in it, Lindsay, using it incorrectly, inaccurately.
sentences.zh: 而且正如卡罗指出的那样——因为卡罗忍不住要挖苦一下——林赛用得并不准确，不恰当。

sentences.en: Like he's, he's blaming Moses for things that were not Moses' problem, you know.
sentences.zh: 他把那些根本不是摩西造成的问题归咎于摩西，你知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, which is, which is amazing when you think about this book, you know,
sentences.zh: 我是说，当你想到这本书时，这真的很神奇，你知道，

sentences.en: dedicated to blaming Moses for most things, you know, like.
sentences.zh: 这本书致力于把大部分事情归咎于摩西，你知道，就像。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, but like still, you know, to his credit, Carol is like, but you can't blame him for the wrong things.
sentences.zh: 但，但即便如此，你知道，卡罗值得称赞的一点是，他会说：你不能把错误的账算在他头上。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like you have to get it right.
sentences.zh: 你得把事实搞清楚。

sentences.en: Like it's not the, it's not the sort of like direction of the sentiment that, that he has a problem with when it comes to Lindsay.
sentences.zh: 他并不是对林赛那种情绪的方向有意见。

sentences.en: He just has a problem with its inaccuracy, which is, which is another sort of speaks to, you know, how great Robert Caro is.
sentences.zh: 他只是对这种不准确性有意见，这又从侧面说明了罗伯特·卡罗有多伟大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's like, we got to dislike him for the right reasons.
sentences.zh: 他就像是说，我们得为了正确的理由去讨厌他。

sentences.en: I don't want to just dislike him.
sentences.zh: 我不想只是单纯地讨厌他。

sentences.en: We got to blame him for the right things.
sentences.zh: 我们得为了正确的事情去责怪他。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is when Moses has this very strange brief epilogue to his, like, not quite afterlife, because he's still alive, but he has nothing to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是摩西人生中那段非常奇怪且短暂的尾声，不算完全的“身后事”，因为他还活着，但他已经无事可做了。

sentences.en: And he gets hired by WPIX.
sentences.zh: 然后他被 WPIX 电视台聘用了。

sentences.en: When I was growing up, they were in New York's movie station.
sentences.zh: 我成长的时候，他们是纽约的电影频道。

sentences.en: Eventually they became part of the, I guess they're part of the CW now.
sentences.zh: 最终他们成了，我想他们现在应该是 CW 电视台的一部分了。

sentences.en: But he briefly hosts a TV discussion show called New York Close-Up, which I think is so strange that someone was like, 81-year-old Robert Moses,
sentences.zh: 但他曾短暂主持过一个名为《纽约特写》的电视访谈节目，我觉得这太奇怪了，居然有人会找 81 岁的罗伯特·摩西，

sentences.en: you were the lead construction guy in all this, in all the city and state.
sentences.zh: 你可是整个城市和州所有这些建设项目的总负责人。

sentences.en: Why don't you host a TV interview, a local TV interview show?
sentences.zh: 为什么不让你来主持一个电视访谈节目，一个本地的电视访谈节目呢？

sentences.en: But he won't wear his hearing aid, so he can't hear his guests while they're taping, and he just lectures at the camera mostly, and they cancel it after 20 episodes.
sentences.zh: 但他不肯戴助听器，所以录制时根本听不见嘉宾在说什么，他大多时候只是对着镜头说教，结果节目播了 20 集就被砍了。

sentences.en: And I got to find an episode of this.
sentences.zh: 我得找一集来看看。

sentences.en: I think there might be some on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我想 YouTube 上可能有一些。

sentences.en: There's a few on YouTube.
sentences.zh: YouTube 上确实有几集。

sentences.en: I was like, I was thinking, I was like, next season on The Power Broker Breakdown, we cover every episode of New York Close-Up.
sentences.zh: 我当时就在想，下一季的《权力掮客》深度解析，我们要把《纽约特写》的每一集都讲一遍。

sentences.en: This is the 99% Invisible Close-Up on New York Close-Up.
sentences.zh: 这就是《99% 隐形》对《纽约特写》的“特写”。

sentences.en: We're covering every episode of New York Close-Up.
sentences.zh: 我们要涵盖《纽约特写》的每一集。

sentences.en: And us watching it, they're talking about local issues that we don't understand at all.
sentences.zh: 我们看的时候，他们谈论的都是我们完全听不懂的本地议题。

sentences.en: We don't know any of the names they're using.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不知道他们提到的那些人名。

sentences.en: But I love the idea of Robert Moses as a talk show hoSt.
sentences.zh: 但我很喜欢罗伯特·摩西担任脱口秀主持人的这个点子。

sentences.en: I find that very, it's just a strange thing for him to be doing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常……他做这种事真的很奇怪。

sentences.en: It's amazing to imagine a more checked out Charlie Rose, you know, kind of just sitting there in a dark room.
sentences.zh: 很难想象一个比查理·罗斯更心不在焉的人，你知道，就坐在那间昏暗的屋子里。

sentences.en: And he's just looking for things to do with his mind.
sentences.zh: 他只是在为自己的大脑寻找消遣。

sentences.en: It's not even the time, it's this mind.
sentences.zh: 这甚至不是时间的问题，而是思想的问题。

sentences.en: And so strangers that he would not have made time for before, they're like, hey, we have an idea for a project in another country.
sentences.zh: 于是，那些他以前根本不会花时间理会的陌生人，跑来跟他说，嘿，我们在另一个国家有个项目构想。

sentences.en: Will you talk to us?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我们谈谈吗？

sentences.en: He's like, yeah, sure, of course, of course.
sentences.zh: 他会说，好啊，当然，当然。

sentences.en: And he gets really into it.
sentences.zh: 而且他真的投入进去了。

sentences.en: Rockefeller eventually leaves office to run for president.
sentences.zh: 洛克菲勒最终离职去竞选总统了。

sentences.en: He doesn't win.
sentences.zh: 他没选上。

sentences.en: There was no president Rockefeller.
sentences.zh: 并没有所谓的洛克菲勒总统。

sentences.en: And the new governor, he offers Moses a post as a housing advisor, which he turns down.
sentences.zh: 新任州长邀请摩西担任住房顾问，但他拒绝了。

sentences.en: And that's when the Moses men, they're dying of old age around him.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，摩西身边的那些老部下们，正一个个因年迈而离世。

sentences.en: It's amazing.
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了。

sentences.en: Sid Shapiro, he still runs the Long Island State Park Commission.
sentences.zh: 西德·夏皮罗，他依然掌管着长岛州立公园委员会。

sentences.en: He's still devoted to Moses.
sentences.zh: 他依然对摩西忠心耿耿。

sentences.en: He makes sure that Moses is treated with reverence at the facilities that the Parks Commission patrolmen are still afraid of him.
sentences.zh: 他确保摩西在那些设施里受到尊崇，以至于公园委员会的巡逻人员至今仍对他心存畏惧。

sentences.en: But when he retires, he was placed by someone from the National Park Service who doesn't care about Moses.
sentences.zh: 但他退休后，接替他的是一位来自国家公园管理局的人，那个人根本不在乎摩西。

sentences.en: And Moses loses his corner table at Jones Beach.
sentences.zh: 于是摩西失去了他在琼斯海滩的专属餐桌。

sentences.en: Guy Lombardo stops introducing him at the Marine Theater.
sentences.zh: 盖伊·隆巴多也不再在海洋剧院介绍他出场了。

sentences.en: And Shapiro dies in 1972.
sentences.zh: 1972 年，夏皮罗去世了。

sentences.en: And Moses' most loyal aide has just gone for good.
sentences.zh: 摩西最忠诚的助手就这样永远离开了。

sentences.en: You know, he's died.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他去世了。

sentences.en: And that in the notes later on, Carol makes it clear that Sid Shapiro had said, don't quote me on any of these things until I die.
sentences.zh: 在后来的笔记中，卡罗明确表示，西德·夏皮罗曾说过，在我死之前，不要引用我说的任何话。

sentences.en: I don't think realizing that he was going to die before the book came out.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他当时意识到自己会在书出版前就去世了。

sentences.en: So just use all of it, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管把这些都用上吧，你知道。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

sentences.en: There's just the last little bit about, you know, the fact that Moses, you know, doesn't have a much of a family legacy.
sentences.zh: 最后还有一点，你知道，摩西并没有留下太多的家族遗产。

sentences.en: You know, like a number of – he has two daughters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，像很多……他有两个女儿。

sentences.en: This is a weird thing about Carol here.
sentences.zh: 关于卡罗的这一点很奇怪。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Is that like he mentions about Moses' grandsons,
sentences.zh: 他是提到了摩西的孙子们，

sentences.en: but he really doesn't get into Moses' granddaughter or – like it's such a – it feels like an old-fashioned thing of like that there's no one to carry on Moses' kind of like lineage in his line.
sentences.zh: 但他真的没怎么提摩西的孙女，或者……这感觉像是一种老派的想法，觉得没有人能继承摩西的血脉。

sentences.en: And when I read it, I kind of wonder, is this a window into Carol, a window into the patriarchy as a whole, or is he putting on the sort of like these people, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我读到这里时，我有点好奇，这是否反映了卡罗的视角，或者是整个父权制的缩影，又或者他是在暗示，这些人，你知道，

sentences.en: his progeny aren't as important to Moses?
sentences.zh: 他的后代对摩西来说并不重要？

sentences.en: You know, he's sort of saying that, you know, like it really requires some kind of male heir to be important to Moses.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他似乎是在说，摩西认为只有男性继承人才是重要的。

sentences.en: I kind of think it's that, but it is sort of – it's odd, you know, what gets sort of paid attention to and what doesn't here.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于这么认为，但这确实有点……奇怪，你知道，这里什么被关注了，什么被忽略了。

sentences.en: Well, I think there's also – I think it – yeah, that's true.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得还有——我觉得它——是啊，确实如此。

sentences.en: It would make more sense to me if it was covering all of his grandchildren or none of his grandchildren, but Carol, I think in keeping with this theme of old,
sentences.zh: 如果他能涵盖所有的孙辈，或者一个都不提，对我来说会更合理，但卡罗，我认为是为了契合这种衰老的基调，

sentences.en: kind of like the disappointments of his old age, that Moses has a couple of grandsons.
sentences.zh: 那种晚年的失落感，摩西有几个孙子。

sentences.en: One of them is born with mental disabilities.
sentences.zh: 其中一个出生时就有智力障碍。

sentences.en: That's the one who's named for him.
sentences.zh: 那个孩子还是以他的名字命名的。

sentences.en: He has one who becomes a banker, and Moses just seems to not be interested in him.
sentences.zh: 他还有一个孙子成了银行家，但摩西似乎对他并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And the third grandson is very charming, but he has bad grades.
sentences.zh: 第三个孙子很有魅力，但成绩很差。

sentences.en: And Carol compares him to Moses' granddaughter, Caroline, who gets very good grades.
sentences.zh: 卡罗把他和摩西的孙女卡罗琳做了对比，卡罗琳的成绩非常好。

sentences.en: And that's the only mention of Caroline that we get.
sentences.zh: 而那也是我们唯一一次看到关于卡罗琳的提及。

sentences.en: I'm like, well, let's hear about her.
sentences.zh: 我就想，好吧，让我们多听听关于她的事吧。

sentences.en: She seems accomplished.
sentences.zh: 她看起来很有成就。

sentences.en: But Moses dotes on this grandson, and when his grades turn around in college, he's really proud of him,
sentences.zh: 但摩西对这个孙子宠爱有加，当他在大学里成绩好转时，摩西真的为他感到骄傲，

sentences.en: that this is maybe the person he's looking to – not even necessarily to continue his tradition of power brokering, but just that brings life to him in his old age.
sentences.zh: 这或许就是他所期待的人——甚至不一定是期待他继续自己的权力掮客传统，只是觉得他在晚年为自己带来了活力。

sentences.en: And then very tragically, this grandson dies in 1968 at the age of 21 in a car accident.
sentences.zh: 然后非常不幸的是，这个孙子在 1968 年因车祸去世了，年仅 21 岁。

sentences.en: And Carol, thankfully, is too good a writer to make a big deal out of, you know, live by the car, die by the car.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，卡罗是一位足够优秀的作家，没有大肆渲染那种“因车而生，因车而死”的讽刺感。

sentences.en: You know how ironic it is that it was a road accident that took the life of his beloved grandson.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他心爱的孙子死于车祸，这有多么讽刺。

sentences.en: But there's this feeling of – I think he brings it up to really hit home the idea that Moses has done all these things, but in a real way,
sentences.zh: 但有一种感觉——我觉得他提这件事是为了强调一个事实：摩西虽然做了那么多事，但在现实层面，

sentences.en: he is leaving nothing behind him for himself or feels like he has nothing left, you know, and that even the thing that brings him joy in his old age is taken from him just by life.
sentences.zh: 他并没有为自己留下什么，或者说他觉得一无所有，你知道，甚至连他在晚年带给他快乐的东西，也被生活夺走了。

sentences.en: You know, that's my guess anyway,
sentences.zh: 你知道，反正我是这么猜的，

sentences.en: but it's a – it sometimes feels – this is one of the few real criticisms I'll make about Carol in some ways is that when he goes – when he does talk about Moses' family,
sentences.zh: 但这确实……有时感觉——这是我唯一会对卡罗提出的一些真正批评，在某些方面，当他谈到摩西的家庭时，

sentences.en: if there's not a way to tie it directly to Moses' work, it often feels like a little bit of an appendage that doesn't need to be there, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果不能直接与摩西的工作挂钩，它往往感觉像是一个没必要存在的附录，你知道，

sentences.en: and something that Carol is clearly not as interested in.
sentences.zh: 而且卡罗显然对这些内容没那么感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are often the sections of the family are little end sections of other chapters where you go like the whole chapter is about something else,
sentences.zh: 是的，关于家庭的部分通常是其他章节末尾的小节，你会觉得整章都在讲别的事，

sentences.en: kind of like the one earlier in this episode where the whole chapter is about something else and the death of Mary is handled in a few pages.
sentences.zh: 就像本集前面提到的那样，整章都在讲别的事，而玛丽的去世只用了几页纸就处理完了。

sentences.en: That's why the one about Paul, the two brothers chapters, stands out so greatly in the book,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么关于保罗的那一章，即两兄弟的那一章，在书中显得如此突出，

sentences.en: like why it's really notable is to spend this whole chapter on the real relationship between these two men in a full fleshed out way.
sentences.zh: 之所以引人注目，是因为他花了一整章的篇幅，以一种非常饱满的方式展现了这两个男人之间真实的关系。

sentences.en: And also why this chapter is also kind of – it has its details about civic life, but mostly it's about the personal sort of – I don't know, the sort of diminishment of the man,
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么这一章也有些……它虽然有关于公民生活的细节，但主要还是关于个人的那种——我不知道，那种人的衰落，

sentences.en: Robert Moses, over the course of the last few years.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·摩西，在最后几年的历程。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not just a sad sack, he's still mean as hell to his secretary, his chauffeur, you know, he takes it out on them.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他不仅仅是个可怜虫，他对秘书、司机依然刻薄得要命，你知道，他把气都撒在他们身上。

sentences.en: The tone of Mayor Lindsay is beginning to sort of catch on in the world, and so he's beginning to be thought of as the person who made things bad in New York.
sentences.zh: 林赛市长的基调开始在世界上流行起来，所以他开始被认为是那个让纽约变糟的人。

sentences.en: And Robert Moses is alive and aware enough to witness some of that turn against him.
sentences.zh: 而罗伯特·摩西还活着，并且清醒地目睹了这种针对他的转变。

sentences.en: Yes, he knows, I think, by this point – I mean, he certainly does after the book comes out.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想他到这个时候已经知道了——我是说，书出版后他肯定知道了。

sentences.en: But he knows, I think, by this point or has an inkling that this name that for so much of his life has meant achievement and power and respect,
sentences.zh: 但我认为他到这个时候已经知道，或者隐约感觉到，这个名字在他大半生中代表着成就、权力和尊重，

sentences.en: that name is now going to mean – not incompetence exactly, but like cruelty, authoritarian domination, waste.
sentences.zh: 而现在这个名字将意味着——不完全是无能，而是残忍、独裁统治、浪费。

sentences.en: His name is now standing for things that he never thought it was going to, and he's aware enough to know that, and he feels it very greatly.
sentences.zh: 他的名字现在代表着他从未想过会代表的东西，他清醒地意识到了这一点，并且感受到了巨大的痛苦。

sentences.en: And it feels like Carol is suggesting this is what is kind of obsessing him towards the end of his life.
sentences.zh: 感觉卡罗是在暗示，这就是他生命尽头所执着的东西。

sentences.en: And the book does not end with his death because this book came out before he died.
sentences.zh: 这本书并没有以他的死亡告终，因为这本书在他去世前就出版了。

sentences.en: He would live for another number of years.
sentences.zh: 他后来又活了许多年。

sentences.en: But the very end of the book I think we should read because it sums up so much about what's going on, and again, it's so beautifully written.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们应该读读这本书的结尾，因为它总结了太多正在发生的事情，而且再次强调，它写得太美了。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: Boom.
sentences.zh: 砰。

sentences.en: Boom.
sentences.zh: 砰。

sentences.en: He has done so much to hurt so many people.
sentences.zh: 他做了那么多伤害那么多人的事。

sentences.en: And the last thought that Carol leaves us with, this thought that's obsessing him is, or that we're led to believe is, why weren't they grateful?
sentences.zh: 而卡罗留给我们的最后一个念头，那个让他执着的念头，或者说让我们相信的念头是：为什么他们不感恩呢？

sentences.en: Why don't they see what they've done and understand it?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们看不到自己所做的一切并理解它呢？

sentences.en: I did so much for you, and now you're going to think of me as the villain.
sentences.zh: 我为你们做了那么多，现在你们却要把我当成恶棍。

sentences.en: But I was the hero, that fundamental need that all humans have to feel like they are the hero in the story of, I mean, their lives and also in most cases of New York City.
sentences.zh: 但我才是英雄，这是所有人内心深处的一种基本需求，即感觉自己是故事中的英雄，我是说，在他们的人生中，在大多数情况下也是在纽约市的故事中。

sentences.en: And to know that this is not going to be the way that he is remembered, most likely.
sentences.zh: 并且意识到，这很可能不会是他被铭记的方式。

sentences.en: And why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Didn't I do so much for you?
sentences.zh: 我难道没有为你们做很多吗？

sentences.en: It's such a – what I like is that it's – Carol has made me feel bad for Moses all through this chapter,
sentences.zh: 这真是……我喜欢的是，它——卡罗在这一整章里让我为摩西感到难过，

sentences.en: partly because it's a thing we're all going to go through if we're lucky of getting older and dealing with age.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，如果我们幸运的话，我们所有人都会经历变老和面对衰老的过程。

sentences.en: But then at the very end, he puts that in, and I'm like, come on, Moses.
sentences.zh: 但在最后，他写下了那段话，我心想，得了吧，摩西。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 得了吧。

sentences.en: Like, this is – that twist at the end of like, without saying it outright, kind of turning you – at least when I'm reading it, turning me around on him all of a sudden again.
sentences.zh: 就像是——结尾的那个转折，在没有明说的情况下，让你——至少在我读的时候，突然又让我对他改观了。

sentences.en: And it's – I think it's just masterful.
sentences.zh: 而且它——我觉得这简直是大师之作。

sentences.en: But also, Roman, what do you think he means by all that?
sentences.zh: 但还有，罗曼，你觉得他那番话是什么意思？

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: What is he saying?
sentences.zh: 他在说什么？

sentences.en: Why aren't they grateful?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不感恩？

sentences.en: Why aren't they grateful?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不感恩？

sentences.en: I mean, it's sort of – I mean, he sort of states it so well.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这有点——我是说，他陈述得太好了。

sentences.en: It's such a great moment where he really just was this man who had no ability to change.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常精彩的时刻，他真的就是一个完全无法改变的男人。

sentences.en: He had the same arrogance that a lot of people that you witness in today's world.
sentences.zh: 他有着和你在当今世界见到的许多人一样的傲慢。

sentences.en: And he mentions – Carol mentioned this with Rockefeller.
sentences.zh: 他提到——卡罗在洛克菲勒那一章提过这个。

sentences.en: He was like, it's like, if I want it, then it is good.
sentences.zh: 他说，就像是，如果我想要它，那它就是好的。

sentences.en: That's like the basis of his – the way his mind works.
sentences.zh: 这就是他思维方式的基础。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: I mean, coming as an idea from me means that it is good for everyone and they should just be thankful that I'm here in the world to make it happen, you know?
sentences.zh: 我是说，作为一个由我提出的想法，意味着它对每个人都是好的，他们应该为我来到这个世界上实现它而感到庆幸，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And he can't see the world any other different way.
sentences.zh: 他无法以任何其他方式看待世界。

sentences.en: Like, he's that solipsistic.
sentences.zh: 他就是那么唯我论。

sentences.en: He's really that arrogant.
sentences.zh: 他真的就是那么傲慢。

sentences.en: It's the source of his power, but it's also the source of why this moment is so terrible for him.
sentences.zh: 这是他权力的来源，但也是为什么这一刻对他来说如此可怕的原因。

sentences.en: Like, it reminds me, strangely, of the movie Jacob's Ladder.
sentences.zh: 就像，它奇怪地让我想起了电影《异世浮生》。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's explain.
sentences.zh: 让我们解释一下。

sentences.en: Let's unpack this because I'm not seeing it right off the top of my head.
sentences.zh: 让我们剖析一下，因为我一时还没看出来。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, there's this –
sentences.zh: 嗯，有这么一个——

sentences.en: Tim Robbins.
sentences.zh: 蒂姆·罗宾斯。

sentences.en: He's going through kind of like a hellish New York.
sentences.zh: 他正在经历一种地狱般的纽约。

sentences.en: He's going through a hellish New York.
sentences.zh: 他正在经历一种地狱般的纽约。

sentences.en: And it turns out – spoiler alert for Jacob's Ladder.
sentences.zh: 结果发现——《异世浮生》剧透预警。

sentences.en: Like, he died in –
sentences.zh: 就像，他死在——

sentences.en: His movie is like 35 years old.
sentences.zh: 他的电影大概有 35 年历史了。

sentences.en: He died in Vietnam and his life that's happening afterward is all just a dream that's happening in kind of an instant as he's dying.
sentences.zh: 他死在越南，之后发生的一切都只是他在临死前瞬间做的一场梦。

sentences.en: It's your classic occurrence at Elk Creek Bridge.
sentences.zh: 这是经典的《猫头鹰溪桥往事》桥段。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that is happening is – so what's his name?
sentences.zh: 所以其中发生的事情是——那么他叫什么名字？

sentences.en: The chiropractor.
sentences.zh: 那个脊椎按摩师。

sentences.en: He's a famous character actor.
sentences.zh: 他是个著名的性格演员。

sentences.en: Aiello.
sentences.zh: 艾耶洛。

sentences.en: Danny Aiello?
sentences.zh: 丹尼·艾耶洛？

sentences.en: Danny Aiello.
sentences.zh: 丹尼·艾耶洛。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's a sort of alternative care therapist and he's talking to him about the fact that, like, he's starting to see nightmares.
sentences.zh: 他是一位另类护理治疗师，他正在和对方谈论他开始出现噩梦的事实。

sentences.en: He's starting to see his world ripped apart because he's dying and he doesn't know it.
sentences.zh: 他开始眼睁睁看着自己的世界分崩离析，因为他快要死了，但他自己却不知道。

sentences.en: So anyway, so this is going to be a long ass aside.
sentences.zh: 总之，这会是一段很长的题外话。

sentences.en: I don't know why we're doing it at the end of this.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么我们要在这本书的结尾聊这个。

sentences.en: But let me just finish.
sentences.zh: 但请让我说完。

sentences.en: But one of the things that Danny Aiello says to him is like, when you're trying to hold on and you have these parts of your life ripped away from you,
sentences.zh: 丹尼·艾洛（Danny Aiello）对他说的其中一件事是，当你试图坚持下去，而你生命中的这些部分却被硬生生剥离时，

sentences.en: those people ripping away from you are demons and they are taking chunks out of who you are.
sentences.zh: 那些从你身边夺走一切的人就是恶魔，他们正在从你的生命中剜去一块块血肉。

sentences.en: But if you accept that you're moving on, you realize that they're actually angels freeing you from the burden of your life.
sentences.zh: 但如果你接受自己正在向前迈进，你就会意识到，他们其实是天使，正在将你从生活的重负中解脱出来。

sentences.en: And it sticks with me, this idea of, like, gracefully going transitioning into a different stage in your life
sentences.zh: 这句话一直萦绕在我心头，这种优雅地过渡到人生不同阶段的想法，

sentences.en: and realizing that having a lot of these things removed from you are actually, like, it's actually good if you just have a different mindset.
sentences.zh: 并意识到，如果你换一种心态，失去很多东西其实是一件好事。

sentences.en: But, like, there's nothing about Robert Moses' character that allows him to go gracefully between stages.
sentences.zh: 但是，罗伯特·摩西（Robert Moses）这个人物身上没有任何特质能让他优雅地在不同阶段间转换。

sentences.en: He is one person.
sentences.zh: 他始终如一。

sentences.en: He's been one person the whole time.
sentences.zh: 他自始至终都是同一个人。

sentences.en: And so when these things are taken away from him, they just are these demons and enemies.
sentences.zh: 所以当这些东西被从他身边夺走时，它们就成了恶魔和敌人。

sentences.en: They rip him down.
sentences.zh: 它们将他摧毁。

sentences.en: They bring him down to nothing.
sentences.zh: 它们让他一无所有。

sentences.en: And that is a prison of his own making.
sentences.zh: 而那正是他亲手打造的牢笼。

sentences.en: Like, you don't have to exist that way.
sentences.zh: 其实，你没必要那样活着。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: His life is so built around doing things and getting things done and not about being a person or, you know, existing in a way.
sentences.zh: 他的人生完全建立在做事和达成目标上，而不是关于如何作为一个人，或者说，如何以某种方式存在。

sentences.en: Like, he feels like he is someone who has no self other than to be in constant motion.
sentences.zh: 他觉得除了不断奔波，他自己什么也不是。

sentences.en: And instead of accepting a state of rest at the end of his life, instead he's like, what am I?
sentences.zh: 与其在生命尽头接受一种平静的状态，他反而会问：我是什么？

sentences.en: What am I if I'm not doing things?
sentences.zh: 如果我不做事，我算什么？

sentences.en: What am I?
sentences.zh: 我是什么？

sentences.en: And it speaks to, I think, the questions that he probably put down when he left college.
sentences.zh: 我想，这呼应了他大学毕业时可能提出的那些问题。

sentences.en: Like, when he was a college poet, I'm sure he was pretty introspective at times about things.
sentences.zh: 当他还是个大学诗人时，我相信他有时会对这些事情进行深刻的反思。

sentences.en: And then he left college and he put down those questions and didn't pick them up again, you know, for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 然后他离开了大学，放下了那些问题，余生再也没有捡起过，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, that is the end of the book.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是书的结尾了。

sentences.en: I don't know if it should have ended with a long metaphor with Jacob's Ladder, the 1990s movie by Adrian Lyne.
sentences.zh: 我不知道它是否应该以阿德里安·莱恩（Adrian Lyne）1990年的电影《异世浮生》（Jacob's Ladder）的长隐喻来结束。

sentences.en: It was the only way it could have ended, Raman.
sentences.zh: 那是它唯一的结局方式，拉曼（Raman）。

sentences.en: I will say, we don't want to end exactly that.
sentences.zh: 我想说，我们不想完全以那种方式结束。

sentences.en: I will say, we're not going to cover this in detail.
sentences.zh: 我想说，我们不会详细讨论这个。

sentences.en: But if you have a physical copy of the book and not this newfangled e-book that I don't know if I trust completely.
sentences.zh: 但如果你有纸质版的书，而不是那种我不知道是否完全可信的新式电子书，

sentences.en: I like paper myself.
sentences.zh: 我个人还是喜欢纸质书。

sentences.en: Then you have his acknowledgments, which he calls debts, and then a section called A Note on Sources, and then his bibliography note section.
sentences.zh: 那么你就会看到他的致谢部分，他称之为“债务”，然后是一个叫“资料来源说明”的部分，接着是书目注释部分。

sentences.en: And for the dedicated caro file, there's some really interesting stuff in there.
sentences.zh: 对于忠实的卡罗（Caro）粉丝来说，里面有一些非常有趣的内容。

sentences.en: We're not going to go through it in general.
sentences.zh: 我们不会通篇细读。

sentences.en: But just kind of you get touches of how he actually put this book together.
sentences.zh: 但你可以从中感受到他是如何把这本书拼凑起来的。

sentences.en: He goes out of his way to thank his wife, Ina, and his editor, Robert Gottlieb.
sentences.zh: 他特意感谢了他的妻子伊娜（Ina）和编辑罗伯特·戈特利布（Robert Gottlieb）。

sentences.en: And he mentions that 522 interviews were conducted for this book, some of multiple interviews of the same people.
sentences.zh: 他提到为这本书进行了522次采访，其中有些人还被采访了多次。

sentences.en: But there's just these little hints throughout this section of how he found the things that he found for this,
sentences.zh: 但在这一部分的字里行间，有一些关于他如何找到这些资料的小线索，

sentences.en: what he and Ina looked through and who they talked to and how hard it was.
sentences.zh: 他和伊娜查阅了什么，他们和谁谈过，以及这有多么困难。

sentences.en: And he mentions at one point that he went into this secret Triborough file collection that he was the first person from the general public ever to see.
sentences.zh: 他提到有一次他进入了一个秘密的三区大桥（Triborough）档案库，他是第一个获准进入的普通公众。

sentences.en: And he talks about these other archival sources that seemingly nobody but him and Ina had ever looked in before.
sentences.zh: 他还谈到了其他一些档案来源，似乎除了他和伊娜，从来没有人查阅过。

sentences.en: They found W.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了W.

sentences.en: Kingsland Macy's papers in his family's attic.
sentences.zh: 金斯兰·梅西（Kingsland Macy）家族阁楼里的文件。

sentences.en: And it's like 40 years of the inner workings of the New York State Republican Party, and no one had ever looked at it, it seems, before them.
sentences.zh: 那记录了纽约州共和党40年的内部运作，似乎在他们之前从未有人看过。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I find exciting about this book is that it's this enormous book.
sentences.zh: 这本书让我感到兴奋的一点是，它是一本如此宏大的书。

sentences.en: It's New York in a book, basically, in so many different ways.
sentences.zh: 从很多方面来说，它基本上就是一本关于纽约的书。

sentences.en: Not all of New York, but so much of it.
sentences.zh: 不是整个纽约，但涵盖了太多内容。

sentences.en: But there's this other hidden epic lying underneath the story of this book,
sentences.zh: 但在书的故事之下，还隐藏着另一部史诗，

sentences.en: which is the story of the discovery of how Robert and Ina Caro learned the things they learned to be able to put this together.
sentences.zh: 那就是罗伯特和伊娜·卡罗是如何通过探索，学到了他们所学到的东西，从而能够完成这本书的。

sentences.en: And we've talked about how in a paragraph about all the details of going into building a certain bridge or a certain highway overpass,
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到过，在一段关于建造某座桥梁或高速公路立交桥的细节描述中，

sentences.en: there's so much research that just goes into understanding that and the work of condensing it down and synthesizing.
sentences.zh: 为了理解这些内容并将其浓缩和综合，需要投入大量的研究工作。

sentences.en: And it feels like there's this incredible, just kind of epic tale of how this book came to be that is just kind of lurking beneath the surface of this book.
sentences.zh: 感觉这本书的背后隐藏着一个令人难以置信的史诗般的故事，讲述了这本书是如何诞生的。

sentences.en: And as a writer, I find almost in some ways as exciting or as thrilling to think about.
sentences.zh: 作为一名作家，我发现思考这些过程在某种程度上同样令人兴奋和激动。

sentences.en: And so I really think it's worth, if you like this book a lot, it's worth just kind of skimming through those note sections to get these little bits and pieces of,
sentences.zh: 所以我真的认为，如果你非常喜欢这本书，值得去浏览一下那些注释部分，去捕捉那些点点滴滴，

sentences.en: these little hints of the process of the making of it.
sentences.zh: 那些关于创作过程的小线索。

sentences.en: You don't have to sit there and read it page to page.
sentences.zh: 你不必坐在那里一页一页地读。

sentences.en: Don't read the bibliography one page after another.
sentences.zh: 不要一页接一页地读参考书目。

sentences.en: That's what a person in an insane asylum does.
sentences.zh: 那是精神病院里的人才会做的事。

sentences.en: But I mean, I did it, but you shouldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 我是读了，但你不应该那样做。

sentences.en: But there's just this, there's something in there that I find very inspiring.
sentences.zh: 但里面确实有一些让我感到非常鼓舞的东西。

sentences.en: After this, oh, this kind of like gut punch ending of this whole book, this experience we've been in,
sentences.zh: 在这之后，哦，在整本书这种重击般的结尾之后，在我们共同经历的这段体验之后，

sentences.en: something inspiring about seeing the dedication and the work that went into making this thing and knowing that that's possible.
sentences.zh: 看到为完成这件事所投入的奉献和努力，并知道这是可能的，这本身就很鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: There's another kind of accomplishment besides building a monument out of concrete,
sentences.zh: 除了用混凝土建造纪念碑之外，还有另一种成就，

sentences.en: and that is building a piece of understanding of reality out of words that can then be shared and live on to anyone who has the interest and the drive to read 1,100 pages of text.
sentences.zh: 那就是用文字构建出对现实的理解，这些理解可以被分享，并活在每一个有兴趣和动力去阅读1100页文本的人心中。

sentences.en: The other thing to check out, if that sort of speaks to you, is Robert Caro's book, Working,
sentences.zh: 如果你对这些感兴趣，另一本值得一看的书是罗伯特·卡罗的《工作》（Working），

sentences.en: which the first chapter or two talks a lot about his coming through the archives and being present and trying to get details and information in places where he is kind,
sentences.zh: 前两章详细讲述了他如何查阅档案，如何亲临现场，以及如何在那些他虽然被允许进入，但并不受欢迎且处处受阻的地方获取细节和信息。

sentences.en: he's allowed into, but he's not welcomed and they make it hard on him.
sentences.zh: 那是一段非常有趣的叙述。

sentences.en: And it's a really fun narrative about all that.
sentences.zh: 这本书真的会伴随你很久。

sentences.en: It's just a really, like this book lives with you.
sentences.zh: 它太长了，你知道，我们花了一整年时间来拆解它，但我发现我还是会一直想起它。

sentences.en: It's so, it's so long, you know, like we've had such an incredible year breaking it down, but I find that I'm like, I still think about it all the time.
sentences.zh: 我还没准备好把它放下。

sentences.en: Like I'm not ready to put it to bed.
sentences.zh: 如果你受到了启发，我强烈推荐《工作》这本书。

sentences.en: Like, and if you're inspired, you know, I highly recommend working.
sentences.zh: 我强烈推荐林登·约翰逊（Lyndon Johnson）系列丛书。

sentences.en: I highly recommend the Lyndon Johnson books.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们始终保持着同样敏锐的观察力，展现了一个作为记者的男人所拥有的极具同理心、趣味性和人文关怀的视角。

sentences.en: I think that they keep going with the same really careful eye, this really empathic and interesting and humanist of a man who's a reporter.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他非常擅长他所做的事情。

sentences.en: You know, he's just very good at what he does.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·卡罗是一个独一无二的存在。

sentences.en: He's a, Robert Caro is a singular entity.
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前，我们在本季早期采访的嘉宾之一是迈克·舒尔（Mike Schur），他是《善地》（The Good Place）和《公园与游憩》（Parks and Rec）的创作者，

sentences.en: So before we go, one of our interviews that we did early on in the season was with Mike Schur, who is the creator of A Good Place and creator of Parks and Rec,
sentences.zh: 他也是《办公室》（The Office）的编剧，还是《权势掮客》（The Power Broker）的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: who's a writer on The Office and was a power broker super fan.
sentences.zh: 在我们与他的谈话中，他开始剧透结局，细节之详尽超出了我们想要的程度。

sentences.en: And part of our conversation with him, he begins to spoil the ending in too great a detail that we wanted to put in.
sentences.zh: 他没意识到他太早开始谈论书的结局了。

sentences.en: So he didn't realize that he was coming in too early to interview to talk about the ending of the book.
sentences.zh: 他只是觉得他必须说出来。

sentences.en: And he just felt like he had to talk.
sentences.zh: 我们无法阻止他。

sentences.en: We couldn't stop him.
sentences.zh: 我们无法阻止他。

sentences.en: We couldn't stop him.
sentences.zh: 我们只能在事后拦住他并进行剪辑。

sentences.en: We just had to hold him back afterwards and edit.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，关于《权势掮客》的结局，最后再分享一个想法，这是迈克·舒尔对结局的进一步解读。

sentences.en: So to have one other final thought on the ending of The Power Broker, here's Mike Schur expanding on his thoughts.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己会成为凯撒或尼禄，或者其他什么人。

sentences.en: And he felt like he was going to be, you know, Caesar or Nero or whoever.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己将成为一段永远不会被取代的历史，这就是为什么书的最后一行——剧透预警——如此美丽。

sentences.en: He was going to be a piece of history that would never be displaced, which is why the last line of the book, spoiler alert, is so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 当摩西被赶下台，洛克菲勒接受了他的辞职——这是没人想到会发生的事，这是一个非常精彩的细节——之后，

sentences.en: When after Moses has been drummed out of power and Rockefeller has accepted his resignation, which no one had ever thought to do, which is such a wonderful detail.
sentences.zh: 书的最后一行基本上是说摩西心情非常糟糕。

sentences.en: The last line of the book is basically that Moses is in a very bad mood.
sentences.zh: 书的最后一行是：为什么他们不感恩呢？

sentences.en: And the last line of the book is, why weren't they grateful?
sentences.zh: 他感到困惑，为什么没有更多的人向他顶礼膜拜，向他献上桂冠，并感谢他所做的一切了不起的事情。

sentences.en: He's baffled about why more people aren't sort of bowing down and like throwing laurels at his feet and thanking him for all of the amazing things that he did.

sentences.en: It's such an incredible portrait of a psychosis that you by the time you get to the end of the book, you're you just feel like you have the complete picture of a man.

sentences.en: It gives me chills thinking about the the achievement that that Carol pulled off.
sentences.zh: 作为《权势掮客》拆解系列最后一集的特别嘉宾，我们将再次在演播室采访罗伯特·卡罗。

sentences.en: And as the special guest on this final episode of The Power Broker Breakdown, we're going to talk to Robert Caro again in studio.
sentences.zh: 我不常采访同一个人超过一次，采访三次更是极其罕见，但我很高兴为罗伯特·卡罗破例。

sentences.en: I don't often interview people more than once, three times is a truly rare occurrence, but I happily made an exception for Robert Caro.
sentences.zh: 第一次是在节目的第一集。

sentences.en: First time was the first episode of the show.

sentences.en: And then earlier this fall, Elliot and I recently interviewed Mr. Caro live on stage at the New York Historical Society,
sentences.zh: 当时他们正在举办一个特别展览，庆祝《权势掮客》出版50周年。

sentences.en: You can hear a little bit more about the exhibit as well as our conversation with Mr. Caro at the Society on a recent episode of 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 现在是第三次了，我希望他能成为我们的最后一位嘉宾。

sentences.en: And now for a third time, I wanted him to be our final gueSt.

sentences.en: In my mind, there really was no one else who it could be.
sentences.zh: 你知道我无法相信的是，它已经出版50年了。

sentences.zh: 我真的，我真的无法相信。

sentences.en: I just I just can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来真的很老套。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems really it's corny.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像昨天一样，你知道，这真的很可怕。

sentences.en: It seems like yesterday, you know, and that's really frightening.
sentences.zh: 我希望，我希望我能说这有什么好的。

sentences.en: I wish I wish I could say there's something good about that.
sentences.zh: 这真的很可怕。

sentences.en: It's really frightening.
sentences.zh: 你还没看过纽约那个关于《权势掮客》的展览，对吧？

sentences.en: You haven't seen the exhibit here in New York on The Power Broker, have you?
sentences.zh: 当你，当你在这里的时候，你去看了吗？

sentences.en: When you when you were here, did you go through?
sentences.zh: 我们匆匆看了一眼。

sentences.zh: 是的，我们去看了。

sentences.en: Yeah, we got to we got to look at it.
sentences.zh: 策展人向我们展示了一些亮点。

sentences.en: And the curator showed us some of the highlights of it.
sentences.zh: 但真的，有一些东西，看到你所做的所有真实的工作，这非常令人兴奋，你知道，

sentences.en: But it's really it's there was something it was so it was very exciting to see all the the real the real work that you did, you know,
sentences.zh: 看到你的原始手稿之类的东西，对你来说，我相信那只是你曾经写过的纸张。

sentences.en: to see your original papers and things like that, which to you, I'm sure, are just papers that you wrote on at one point.
sentences.zh: 但对我们来说，它们就像，你知道，就像我们去卢尔德朝圣一样。

sentences.en: But but to us, they're like, you know, it's like we're taking a pilgrimage to Lourdes or something like that.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了那些神圣的文物之类的东西。

sentences.en: We're seeing the the holy artifacts and things.
sentences.zh: 看到那些东西非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: It was very exciting to see that stuff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我对那个策划展览的女士说，你真的想讲述一本书的故事。

sentences.en: You know, it's it's I said to the woman who put it together, you really want to tell the story of a book.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人真正做到过。

sentences.en: Nobody's really done that.
sentences.zh: 她从我写给他的请求授权写书的信开始，到他回信让我“滚蛋”，你知道，

sentences.en: And she starts off with my letter to him asking for permission to do the book and his letter to me saying, basically, fuck off, you know,

sentences.en: goes all the way to the to the good reviews.
sentences.zh: 总之，我不说了，让你们来吧。

sentences.en: Anyway, I'll stop talking and let you guys.
sentences.zh: 好吧，再次感谢你抽出时间与我们交谈。

sentences.en: Well, thank you again for taking the time and speaking with us.
sentences.zh: 能和你在一起，并在拆解《权势掮客》的这段旅程中受到你的加持，真是一种荣幸。

sentences.en: It's just been a real pleasure to be with you and be blessed in this journey of breaking down the power broker.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 在这段旅程中，有你的存在和半授权，真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Having your presence in your semi authorization for us on this journey has been really wonderful.
sentences.zh: 我们非常感激，因为你本可以像摩西先生那样反应。

sentences.en: And we're so thankful for it when you could have reacted the same way that Mr.
sentences.zh: 你本可以轻易地说：我不想参与其中。

sentences.en: Moses did when you got in touch with him.
sentences.zh: 不，谢谢。

sentences.en: You could have easily said, I want no part of this.
sentences.zh: 我的律师会介入的。

sentences.en: No, thank you.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: My lawyers are getting involved.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想从结尾开始。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们之前谈到过你花在开头句和结尾句上的时间。

sentences.en: So I just wanted to start with the end.
sentences.zh: 你花了多久才知道“为什么他们不感恩呢”会成为你的最后一行？

sentences.en: We talked before about how much time you spend on beginning sentences and ending sentences.
sentences.zh: 我很久都不知道。

sentences.en: How long did you know why weren't they grateful was going to be your final line?
sentences.zh: 如果我没有听到这句话，我不知道这本书会写得这么好。

sentences.en: I didn't I didn't know it for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我完成了所有的研究。

sentences.en: And if I hadn't heard it, I don't know that the book would have turned out so well.
sentences.zh: 是时候开始写作了。

sentences.en: I'd finished all my research.
sentences.zh: 我找不到一种方法来整合这些庞大的研究资料。

sentences.en: It was time to start writing.
sentences.zh: 资料实在太多了。

sentences.en: I couldn't find a way to put this vast mass of research together.
sentences.zh: 什么才是统一的主题呢？

sentences.en: There was just too much of it.
sentences.zh: 我真的卡住了。

sentences.en: What was going to be the unifying theme?
sentences.zh: 我真的卡住了。

sentences.en: And I was really stuck.
sentences.zh: 我真的卡住了。

sentences.en: Now, at that time, Moses, of course, had long since stopped talking to me.
sentences.zh: 当时，摩西当然早就已经不跟我说话了。

sentences.en: But whenever he made a public appearance, I would go and sit in the audience.
sentences.zh: 但每当他公开露面时，我都会去坐在观众席里。

sentences.en: And on this particular occasion, when I was really stuck on how to do the book,
sentences.zh: 就在那次，当我真的卡住不知道该怎么写这本书时，

sentences.en: he was dedicating a memorial bench at the 1964 World's Fair.
sentences.zh: 他正在1964年世界博览会上为一座纪念长椅揭幕。

sentences.en: And he got up to give a speech.
sentences.zh: 他起身发表讲话。

sentences.en: And in the first two rows were all the Moses men, his engineers and architects, two rows of gray heads.
sentences.zh: 前两排坐着的都是“摩西的人”，他的工程师和建筑师们，两排灰白的脑袋。

sentences.en: Everybody was getting old.
sentences.zh: 每个人都老了。

sentences.en: And the theme of his talk was the ingratitude of the public toward great men.
sentences.zh: 他演讲的主题是公众对伟人的忘恩负义。

sentences.en: And he said, someday we will sit on this bench and ponder the ingratitude of the public toward great men.
sentences.zh: 他说，总有一天我们会坐在长椅上，思考公众对伟人的忘恩负义。

sentences.en: And I saw all these heads nodding, yes, the commission is right, right as always.
sentences.zh: 我看到那些脑袋都在点头，是的，委员会说得对，一如既往地对。

sentences.en: And I heard someone whisper, yes, why weren't they grateful?
sentences.zh: 我还听到有人低语，是啊，他们为什么不感恩呢？

sentences.en: And when I heard that line, it sounds magical.
sentences.zh: 当我听到那句话时，感觉真是神奇。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, in that moment, the book came together for me.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，就在那一刻，书的构思在我脑海中成型了。

sentences.en: And I knew what was the theme of the whole book and how to organize it.
sentences.zh: 我知道了整本书的主题是什么，也知道该如何组织它。

sentences.en: And I remember I raced back as fast as I could before I went out of my mind to my office and started outlining the book.
sentences.zh: 我记得我以最快的速度赶回办公室，生怕自己忘了，然后就开始列书的提纲。

sentences.en: And it proved to be okay.
sentences.zh: 结果证明这很不错。

sentences.en: The outline proved to be okay.
sentences.zh: 提纲证明是没问题的。

sentences.en: It all, yeah.
sentences.zh: 一切都，没错。

sentences.en: So that was, and ever since then, Elliot and Roman, I learned my lesson.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样，从那以后，埃利奥特和罗曼，我吸取了教训。

sentences.en: I have to have the last line of the book before I start writing.
sentences.zh: 我必须在动笔之前就确定书的最后一行。

sentences.en: I have to know it.
sentences.zh: 我必须知道它。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: As soon as I know it, the book falls into place leading up to it.
sentences.zh: 一旦我知道了，整本书就会顺着它自然而然地铺陈开来。

sentences.en: And each time when you choose that last line, that's the one you stick with?
sentences.zh: 每次当你选定那最后一行，你就会坚持用它吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There aren't times where you're like, eh, I'll change it to something else when I get there.
sentences.zh: 不会有那种时候吗，比如，哎，等我写到那儿再换成别的？

sentences.en: It's just hard and faSt.
sentences.zh: 那是板上钉钉的。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I don't change it.
sentences.zh: 我不会改。

sentences.en: It's deeper than a, you know, deeper than a feeling.
sentences.zh: 这比一种，你知道，比一种感觉要深刻得多。

sentences.en: You suddenly know how the book should be put together.
sentences.zh: 你突然就知道这本书该如何构建了。

sentences.en: It's sort of a wonderful thing.
sentences.zh: 这真是一件美妙的事情。

sentences.en: Now that I know that it will happen if I, you know, sometimes you sit and think about that for several weeks, you know, but when you, yes, when you find things just get better.
sentences.zh: 现在我知道只要我，你知道，有时你会坐下来思考几周，你知道，但当你，是的，当你发现事情只会变得更好。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: As we were reading through the book, so much of the early sections of the book, it feels like you are writing about the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当我们通读这本书时，书的前半部分，感觉就像你在写过去。

sentences.en: You're writing about things that when you were writing were already history.
sentences.zh: 你写的是那些在你动笔时就已经成为历史的事情。

sentences.en: And there's a certain period where it feels like it transitions into contemporary history.
sentences.zh: 有一段时期，感觉它过渡到了当代史。

sentences.en: When you're writing about Mayor Lindsay or about the 1964 World's Fair, you're writing about things that you are experiencing.
sentences.zh: 当你写到林赛市长或1964年世界博览会时，你写的是你亲身经历过的事情。

sentences.en: And I couldn't help but wonder if it felt different writing about these periods that you only knew through research and writing through these periods of Moses' life that you were,
sentences.zh: 我不禁想问，写那些你只通过研究了解的时期，与写那些你——

sentences.en: in many cases, already a working reporter during that time.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，当时已经是在职记者的时期，感觉会有所不同吗？

sentences.en: Did it feel different?
sentences.zh: 感觉不同吗？

sentences.en: It did feel different.
sentences.zh: 确实感觉不同。

sentences.en: It did feel completely different.
sentences.zh: 确实感觉完全不同。

sentences.en: When I was writing the section on Mayor Lindsay and his later efforts to build the bridges and all, I felt that I was writing a contemporary, I was,
sentences.zh: 当我写到林赛市长和他后来努力修建桥梁等等的部分时，我觉得我是在写一部当代，我是在，

sentences.en: I was writing a contemporary story.
sentences.zh: 我是在写一个当代故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And as it became apparent to me that he wasn't going to be, later, that he wasn't going to be restored to power when he had been, while I was writing the book,
sentences.zh: 当后来我明显感觉到他不会，他不会在我在写书的时候重掌大权，

sentences.en: he was removed from power, as you know.
sentences.zh: 他被免职了，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And that's when I started to feel so sorry for him, as if I was thinking, oh, he wants to do all these things, and he has nothing to do.
sentences.zh: 那时我开始为他感到难过，我就在想，噢，他想做所有这些事，却无事可做。

sentences.en: And when one of his aides said to me, as I think is quoted near the end of the book, imagine this great mind, it's as great as ever, and he has nothing to do with it,
sentences.zh: 当他的一位助手对我说，我想书的结尾引用了这句话，想象一下这个伟大的头脑，它依然像以前一样伟大，但他却无处施展，

sentences.en: and nothing to accomplish with it.
sentences.zh: 也没什么能用它来完成的。

sentences.en: But I felt so, the poignance of old age, you know, and the poignance of whatever he had done, however I had judged it, I didn't change my opinion of it,
sentences.zh: 但我感到非常，那种老年的辛酸，你知道，无论我如何评判他所做的一切，我都没有改变我的看法，

sentences.en: but I remember feeling sorrow for what was going on, not what I was writing about in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 但我记得我为正在发生的事情感到悲伤，而不是为我所写的过去。

sentences.en: But there's also a sense in those chapters where I can feel your opinion of Lindsay a little bit, and your opinion of the World's Fair,
sentences.zh: 但在那些章节里，也能感觉到你对林赛的一点看法，以及你对世界博览会的看法，

sentences.en: because you were there to bear witness to it.
sentences.zh: 因为你当时就在现场见证了这一切。

sentences.en: Could you talk about, like, maybe the style in writing to, like, incorporate a little bit more of that firsthand eyewitness account of these people?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈，比如，写作风格上，是否可以更多地融入那种对这些人的第一手目击记录？

sentences.en: Well, that's a terrific question, particularly with the relation to Lindsay, because Lindsay was the darling of the newspapers, you know, he was the darling of the New York Times,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个极好的问题，特别是关于林赛，因为林赛是报纸的宠儿，你知道，他是《纽约时报》的宠儿，

sentences.en: and he had set out, you know, he was going to take Moses's power away from him, you know, and Moses goes up to Albany on another visit, you know, for one day.
sentences.zh: 他曾扬言，你知道，他要从摩西手中夺走权力，你知道，然后摩西又去了一次奥尔巴尼，你知道，就一天。

sentences.en: And at the end of that, Lindsay was the young, bright, very eloquent, talking, you know, parcel of good government, and the old line comes up to Albany, and at the end of it,
sentences.zh: 在那之后，林赛是那个年轻、聪明、口才极佳、谈吐不凡的“良政”代言人，而老派人物来到奥尔巴尼，最后，

sentences.en: Lindsay is finished with his plans, you know.
sentences.zh: 林赛的计划就此终结了，你知道。

sentences.en: It was a great, unbelievable example of Robert Moses's sheer power.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于罗伯特·摩西绝对权力的伟大且令人难以置信的例子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I hadn't thought about it until you compared it to your realization of this is where this power comes from, that in reading that chapter,
sentences.zh: 在你把它与你意识到权力的来源进行比较之前，我还没想到这一点，在读那一章时，

sentences.en: it feels like you are trying to say to Lindsay, come on, like, you don't know what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 感觉你好像在对林赛说，得了吧，你根本不知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: You've got to figure out what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 你得搞清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: This guy knows so much more than you.
sentences.zh: 这家伙比你懂得多得多。

sentences.en: You can't – and there's something so powerful in that, I think, maybe because you are – you're saying to Lindsay, like, I had to go through this realization, like,
sentences.zh: 你不能——我觉得这其中有一种非常强大的力量，也许是因为你——你在对林赛说，就像，我必须经历这种认识，就像，

sentences.en: you need to do this.
sentences.zh: 你需要这样做。

sentences.en: You're the mayor.
sentences.zh: 你是市长。

sentences.en: You know, it feels like if you're getting – there's this frustration with him that is so palpable that I really love in that chapter.
sentences.zh: 你知道，感觉如果你正在——那种对他产生的挫败感是如此明显，我真的很喜欢那一章。

sentences.en: It really feels like you're there watching you get frustrated at this guy who's totally underestimating his opponent.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像你在现场看着你对这个完全低估了对手的家伙感到沮丧。

sentences.en: That's right, because the paper's called Lindsay's victory over Moses, you know.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为报纸称之为林赛战胜了摩西，你知道。

sentences.en: I said, no one understands.
sentences.zh: 我说，没人明白。

sentences.en: This guy has just taken the measure of you.
sentences.zh: 这家伙刚刚摸清了你的底细。

sentences.en: He didn't – it wasn't even hard.
sentences.zh: 他甚至——这根本不费吹灰之力。

sentences.en: What was the quote?
sentences.zh: 那句引语是什么？

sentences.en: You know, it's been so long since I wrote it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我写那本书已经是很久以前的事了。

sentences.en: But someone said something about, you know, he was so handsome.
sentences.zh: 但有人说了些什么，你知道，他长得那么帅。

sentences.en: He was – he talked so well.
sentences.zh: 他——他谈吐那么好。

sentences.en: And someone said something to Moses that's in the book.
sentences.zh: 有人对摩西说了些书里提到的事。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: I didn't have it reread.
sentences.zh: 我没重读过。

sentences.en: We kind of were expecting you to reread the book before the interview.
sentences.zh: 我们本来以为你在采访前会重读这本书的。

sentences.en: But, you know, if you haven't, that's okay.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道，如果你没读，也没关系。

sentences.en: But someone said something like, well, you won.
sentences.zh: 但有人说了类似的话，嗯，你赢了。

sentences.en: It was easy.
